chapter: Boston, Buffalo and finding a style
title: Building stamina and finger strength on the bass
summary: He built strength by playing long nights and practicing daily to strengthen his hands and fingers.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: Now, one of the things I wanted to ask you was, as a -- how did you build up your stamina to play, say like in a jazz band? You know, that's one of the things, stamina-wise, jazz players can play the bass, pizzicato, you know, much better and longer than symphony players. How did you go about building that up? I mean, did you -- is it just from having to play all night or did you really work at having the stamina?

Having to work quite a few hours at night and I did practice quite a bit during the day, you know, my fiddle to develop my strength in my hands and especially my fingers that I plucked with, you know. That helped quite a bit to practice quite, you know, getting my strength in my arms and hands, you know.
Now, were there particular kinds of exercises you did on the bass? Did you do -- what did you do?

Oh, just more or less played my bass and get the notes and keep swinging, swinging, you know, and getting the feel. The more I played it, the more I could feel where I want to place my hands, my fingers to pluck the different strings and finger, finger the different strings.
